UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

      PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., et al.                  )                Docket No. EL26-67-000

    REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION, OR IN THE ALTERNATIVE, REHEARING OF
               THE INDICATED PJM TRANSMISSION OWNERS

        Pursuant to Section 313 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Rules 212 and 713 of the

Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or

“FERC”),2 the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners (“PJM Transmission Owners”)3 respectfully

request clarification, or in the alternative, rehearing of the Commission’s order issued on June 18,

2026, in this proceeding relating to the appropriate definitions of “large load” and “electrically

proximate large load.”4

        On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued show cause orders under section 206 of the FPA

to PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”), Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.,

Southwest Power Pool, Inc., California Independent System Operator Corporation, ISO New

England Inc., and New York Independent System Operator, Inc., together with their transmission

3
          The Indicated PJM Transmission Owners are: American Electric Power Service Corporation on behalf of its
affiliates, Appalachian Power Company, Indiana Michigan Power Company, Kentucky Power Company, Kingsport
Power Company, Ohio Power Company, Wheeling Power Company, AEP Appalachian Transmission Company, Inc.,
AEP Indiana Michigan Transmission Company, Inc., AEP Kentucky Transmission Company, Inc., AEP Ohio
Transmission Company, Inc., and AEP West Virginia Transmission Company, Inc.; The Dayton Power and Light
Company d/b/a AES Ohio; Dominion Energy Services, Inc. on behalf of Virginia Electric and Power Company d/b/a
Dominion Energy Virginia; Duke Energy Business Services, LLC for Duke Energy Kentucky, Inc. and Duke Energy
Ohio, Inc.; Duquesne Light Company; East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Inc.; Exelon Corporation on behalf of its
affiliates Atlantic City Electric Company, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company, Commonwealth Edison Company,
Commonwealth Edison Company of Indiana, Inc., Delmarva Power & Light Company, PECO Energy Company, and
Potomac Electric Power Company; FirstEnergy Service Company, on behalf of its affiliates American Transmission
Systems, Incorporated, Jersey Central Power & Light Company, Mid-Atlantic Interstate Transmission LLC, The
Potomac Edison Company, Monongahela Power Company, Keystone Appalachian Transmission Company, and
Trans-Allegheny Interstate Line Company (collectively, the “FirstEnergy Companies”); PPL Electric Utilities
Corporation; and Rockland Electric Company.
4
        PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,211 (2026) (“PJM Show Cause Order” or “Order”).
 owners,5 directing each region to justify or reform the tariff provisions governing how large loads

connect to and receive service from the transmission system.6

        The PJM Show Cause Order preliminarily found that PJM’s existing Open Access

Transmission Tariff (“PJM Tariff”) appeared to be unjust, unreasonable, or unduly discriminatory

or preferential because of a lack of sufficiently clear and consistent provisions to address service

for large loads and related configurations.7 The Commission therefore directed PJM and its

transmission owners, within 60 days, to show cause why the PJM Tariff remains just and

reasonable without provisions addressing: (1) the application process, study procedures, and

ongoing operational requirements for Eligible Customers8 seeking transmission service on behalf

of large loads; (2) additional transparency concerning Network Upgrade costs for such service,

together with the absence of a pro forma cost recovery agreement and a mechanism to ensure

related payments are properly credited to transmission owners’ revenue requirements; (3)

transmission service options tailored to flexible large loads willing and able to limit their use of

the transmission system under certain conditions; and (4) rates, terms, and conditions applicable

to interconnection customers serving “electrically proximate large load” or co-located load.9 The




5
          Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,212 (2026), Southwest Power Pool, et al.,
195 FERC ¶ 61,213 (2026), California Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,214 (2026), ISO New England
Inc., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,215 (2026), New York Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,216 (2026)
(collectively, the “Show Cause Orders”).
6
         The Commission’s June 18, 2026, show cause orders follow the Secretary of Energy’s letter, pursuant to
section 403 of the Department of Energy Organization Act, directing FERC to initiate a rulemaking proceeding and
to consider its advanced notice of proposed rulemaking (“ANOPR”) to accelerate large load interconnections. See
Letter and ANOPR of Chris Wright, Sec’y, U.S. Dep’t of Energy (Oct. 23, 2025). The Commission subsequently
invited comments on the proposed ANOPR. See Notice Inviting Comments, Docket No. RM26-4-000 (issued Oct.
27, 2025).
7
        PJM Show Cause Order at PP 3, 35.
8
        All capitalized terms that are not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning set forth in the PJM Tariff.
9
        PJM Show Cause Order at PP 3, 35.



                                                          2
 Commission directed PJM either to justify the absence of such provisions or to propose Tariff

revisions addressing those concerns.10

       The PJM Transmission Owners share the underlying goals driving the Commission’s

issuance of the Show Cause Orders: namely, to enable new large load customers to efficiently

interconnect to the transmission system while simultaneously ensuring reliability and protecting

existing customers. To that end, the PJM Transmission Owners respectfully seek clarification, or

in the alternative, rehearing of two preliminary findings in the PJM Show Cause Order:

       1. The Commission should clarify that adopting the definition of “large load” proposed
          in the Show Cause Order, including the 50 MW threshold criteria, does not prevent
          PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners from proposing and supporting additional
          service-specific criteria for large load customers relating to the types of services
          contemplated in the Show Cause Order. If the Commission declines to make this
          clarification, it should grant rehearing, as a one-size-fits-all approach for all customers
          that meet the definition of “large load” is likely to be over-inclusive and unduly
          discriminatory, and undermine the Commission’s speed-to-power goals for large load
          customers, particularly large computational loads that are crucial to serving AI
          processes.

       2. The Commission should clarify that PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners will be
          permitted to propose and support a definition of “large load” and “electrically
          proximate large load” that are not based on the location of facilities relative to the Point
          of Interconnection,11 e.g., by proposing a definition that relies on the Point of Change
          of Ownership. If the Commission declines to adopt this clarification, it should grant
          rehearing. As PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners have explained in the PJM co-
          located load proceeding, there are significant problems with adopting such definitions
          based on facilities on the customer-side of the Point of Interconnection, including
          potentially encouraging gaming activities that will undermine the efficient and reliable
          interconnection of large loads.




10
       PJM Show Cause Order at PP 3, 35.
11
       Id. at P 94 & n.7.



                                                 3
 I.     REQUESTS FOR CLARIFICATION AND REHEARING

       A.       Statement of Issues and Specification of Errors

       To the extent that the Commission declines to grant clarification as set forth below, the

PJM Transmission Owners submit the following Statement of Issues and Specification of Errors

pursuant to Rule 713(c)(1) and 713(c)(2) of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure:12

           To the extent that the definition of “large load” proposed in the PJM Show Cause Order
            is intended to restrict PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners from proposing and
            supporting additional service-specific criteria for large load customers, the PJM Show
            Cause Order is arbitrary and capricious, does not reflect reasoned decision-making, and
            is unsupported by substantial evidence in violation of the Administrative Procedure Act
            because the Commission did not develop a sufficient record to support such a
            restriction, and such a restriction would be unjust, unreasonable, and unduly
            discriminatory. Motor Vehicle Mfrs. Ass’n v. State Farm Mut. Auto Ins. Co., 463 U.S.
            29, 43 (1983) (an agency “must examine the relevant data and articulate a satisfactory
            explanation for its action including a ‘rational connection between the facts found and
            the choice made’”) (citation omitted) (“State Farm”); Consol. Edison Co. of N.Y. v.
            FERC, 45 F.4th 265 (D.C. Cir. 2022); Consol. Edison Co. of N.Y. v. FERC, 347 F.3d
            964, 972 (D.C. Cir. 2003); PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 161 FERC ¶ 61,252 (2017);
            Fla. Gas Transmission Co. v. FERC, 604 F.3d 636, 639 (D.C. Cir. 2010) (quoting Pac.
            Gas & Elec. Co. v. FERC, 373 F.3d 1315, 1319 (D.C. Cir. 2004)) (“Fla. Gas”); PJM
            Interconnection, L.L.C., 119 FERC ¶ 61,318 (2007); Midwest Indep. Transmission Sys.
            Operator, Inc., 117 FERC ¶ 61,113 (2006) (“Midwest ISO”).

           The PJM Show Cause Order is arbitrary and capricious, does not reflect reasoned
            decision-making, and is unsupported by substantial evidence in violation of the
            Administrative Procedure Act because the Commission did not develop a sufficient
            record to support defining “large load” or “electrically proximate large load” by
            reference to the interconnection customer’s point of interconnection. State Farm, 463
            U.S. at 43 (an agency “must examine the relevant data and articulate a satisfactory
            explanation for its action including a ‘rational connection between the facts found and
            the choice made’”) (citation omitted); Consol. Edison Co. of N.Y. v. FERC, 45 F.4th
            265; Consol. Edison Co. of N.Y. v. FERC, 347 F.3d at 972; PJM Interconnection,
            L.L.C., 161 FERC ¶ 61,252; Fla. Gas, 604 F.3d at 639 (quoting Pac. Gas & Elec. Co.
            v. FERC, 373 F.3d at 1319); PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 119 FERC ¶ 61,318;
            Midwest ISO, 117 FERC ¶ 61,113.




12
       18 C.F.R. § 385.713(c)(1), (c)(2).



                                                 4
        B.        Arguments

                 1.     The Commission Should Clarify That the Proposed Definition of
                        “Large Load” in the Show Cause Order Does not Limit PJM and the
                        PJM Transmission Owners From Proposing Additional Service-
                        Specific Criteria for the Services Contemplated in the Order.

       In the PJM Show Cause Order, the Commission preliminarily found that the PJM Tariff

appears unjust and unreasonable because it lacks certain provisions governing the process to

provide transmission service to Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads, including a definition

of large load, as a new category of load. The Commission further stated that, based on the ANOPR

record, it would be reasonable to define a large load as a new commercial or industrial customer

at a single site, behind one or more points of interconnection, with a peak load of 50 MW or greater,

interconnected at a voltage above 69 kV, and not part of a co-location arrangement. The

Commission therefore directed PJM either to show cause why the PJM Tariff remains just and

reasonable without such a definition or to propose tariff revisions establishing its own definition

of large load.

       The Commission should clarify that this definition, including the 50 MW threshold, does

not limit PJM or the PJM Transmission Owners from proposing additional criteria or reasonable

distinctions between large load customers for purposes of designing and implementing the

products addressed in the Order. It may not be appropriate to offer identical services to all large

load customers. For instance, considerations such as seasonality versus peak load measurements

and functional distinctions between types of customers (e.g., hyperscale computational loads

versus “traditional” manufacturing and commercial customers) may merit distinctions in how

different products are designed, offered and priced. The Commission therefore should clarify that

the proposed large load definition does not prejudge the appropriate criteria for every other purpose

under the PJM Tariff.



                                                 5
         If the Commission declines to adopt this clarification, the Commission should grant

rehearing. The PJM Show Cause Order fails to justify a conclusion that the proposed large load

definition requires that every customer meeting the definition of large load must be offered the

same services under the same rates, terms and conditions.13 To the contrary, requiring a one-size-

fits all approach for all large load customers with respect to each new service is likely to undermine

the goals of the Show Cause Order, particularly the desire for speed-to-power. As the PJM

Transmission Owners explained in their comments on the ANOPR, an overly inclusive definition

of “large load” risks repeating the same flaws that occurred with inflated generation

interconnection queues.14 It is therefore of critical importance that PJM and the PJM Transmission

Owners have sufficient flexibility to design and implement services with appropriate criteria that

account for meaningful differences between large load customers. Limiting this flexibility would

be arbitrary, capricious, and would not reflect reasoned decision-making.

                2.      The Commission Should Clarify That “Large Load” and “Electrically
                        Proximate Large Load” Need not be Defined Based on the Point of
                        Interconnection.

        As noted above, the Commission indicated in the PJM Show Cause Order that it would be

reasonable to define a large load as a new commercial or industrial customer at a single site, behind

one or more points of interconnection.15 Similarly, in discussing potential rules and procedures

relating to “electrically proximate large load,” the Commission found that it would be reasonable

to define “electrically proximate large load” as a large load that is sufficiently electrically close to

the interconnection customer’s requested point of interconnection such that, with the exception of

the transmission facilities between the two, the impact on the transmission system of the


13
        PJM Show Cause Order at P 58.
14
        Indicated PJM Transmission Owners Comments, Docket No. RM26-4-000, at 4-9 (filed Nov. 21, 2025).
15
        PJM Show Cause Order at n.2.



                                                    6
 combination of the generating facility and load will be effectively the same as if they were located

at the same substation.16

        The Commission should clarify that in any Section 205 filing or other response to the PJM

Show Cause Order, PJM and/or the PJM Transmission Owners are not limited to defining “large

load” or “electrically proximate large load” based on reference to the point of interconnection, and

that they will have sufficient flexibility to propose other points of reference, such as the Point of

Change of Ownership. Given the significant detail that the Show Cause Order leaves to PJM and

the PJM Transmission Owners to develop as to what constitutes electrical proximity and other

aspects of the Show Cause Order’s proposal, it is crucial that PJM and the PJM Transmission

Owners have maximum flexibility to ensure speed-to-power, reliability, and customer protection

goals are met. Indeed, the Commission has already been presented, in the related co-located load

proceeding, with evidence that the point of interconnection frequently is an imprecise boundary

insofar as it may unreasonably conflate customer-owned facilities with those owned by other

entities, including Transmission Owner-owned facilities.17 In that proceeding, PJM and the PJM

Transmission Owners provided evidence that the definition of “Co-Located Load” should be based

on the Point of Change in Ownership,18 rather than the Point of Interconnection because it reflects

the legal and operational boundary between customer-owned facilities and transmission owner

facilities and avoids sweeping in transmission owner interconnection facilities into the definition




16
        Id. at P 94.

Compliance Filing”); see also PJM Transmission Owners Request for Rehearing or Clarification, Docket No. ER26-
1088-000, at 4-8 (filed May 18, 2026); PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 195 FERC ¶ 61,030, at PP 27-28 (2026).
18
         PJM defined “Point of Change in Ownership” in Tariff, Part VIII, Subpart A, section 400, Definitions P, is
the point at which “the Project Developer’s Interconnection Facilities connect to the Transmission Owner’s
Interconnection Facilities.” See 30-Day Compliance Filing at n.14.



                                                        7
 of large load.19 The Commission has, to date, rejected PJM’s proposal to define Co-Located Load

based on the Point of Change of Ownership because PJM did not seek rehearing or clarification of

the Commission’s order in the separate co-located load proceeding in which it adopted that

definition.20 That rejection is inapt here because the services that the Commission is proposing in

the Show Cause Order involve different customers (i.e., Co-Located Load customers versus other

types of large load customers), and thus, PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners cannot be limited

in responding to Show Cause Order based on the Co-Located Load dockets.

        Furthermore, the PJM Transmission Owners are not asking the Commission to decide at

this time in this proceeding whether the point of interconnection or some other criteria should be

used to define “large loads” or “electrically proximate large loads.” Nevertheless, the Commission

should clarify that the PJM Show Cause Order does not require reference to the point of

interconnection, and that PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners may, in a Section 205 filing or

other response to the Order, propose other criteria, subject of course to showing they are just and

reasonable. If the Commission declines to grant this clarification, it should grant rehearing on this

issue. The PJM Show Cause Order does not explain why the point of interconnection is the

appropriate criterion for PJM, as opposed to other metrics such as ownership, delivery

configuration, voltage, or operational effect on the transmission system. Any determination that a

large load customer or electrically proximate large load customer must be defined based only on

reference to the point of interconnection is therefore not based on reasoned decision-making and

is not supported by substantial evidence.

                                                      8
 II.     CONCLUSION

        For the foregoing reasons, the PJM Transmission Owners respectfully request that the

Commission grant rehearing of the PJM Show Cause Order for the reasons set forth herein, or,

alternatively, clarify the Order as set forth in Section I.



                                                Respectfully submitted,
